meaning: to suddenly feel too nervous or scared to do something you had planned
example: He got cold feet before his speech and asked someone else to give it.
origin: Possibly from the physical sensation of cold feet caused by fear or nerves; the exact origin is uncertain

wrong_meanings.meaning: to have very cold feet because of the weather
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal meaning, not the idiomatic one.
The idiom has nothing to do with walking or snow.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to become very angry all of a sudden
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes fear or nervousness, not anger.

explanation: 'Get cold feet' describes the moment when fear or nerves make a person want to back out of a plan they had already agreed to.
